## Your chosen setup: Azure Container Apps, 1 replica per service, 1 service, no separate load balancer

**In plain words.** Microsoft runs your containers for you. There are no machines or clusters to look after, and it comes with its own web address and HTTPS.

**Cost.** About 23.92 EUR per month. From Azure's own price list for West Europe (read 2026-11-14): Container Apps at the full running rate for the whole month, converted to EUR, excluding VAT. Azure charges less while a copy is idle and gives a free allowance each month, so your real bill can be lower. Traffic out of Azure is not included.

**If the machine or its data centre has a problem:** this stops until it's fixed or recreated, because everything runs in one place.

**What you get**

- No servers or clusters to look after: you hand over a container and it runs.
- It comes with an HTTPS entry point, so there is no separate load balancer to pay for.
- Can add and remove copies as traffic changes, once you set the scaling rules.
- Other Azure services, like a managed database, sit in the same account.

**Why it costs what it does.** It costs more than one machine because every copy of your app is paid for each second it runs. The report prices the copies at their full running rate; Azure charges less while a copy is idle and gives a free allowance each month, so your real bill can be lower.

**What you give up**

- The report prices the copies at their full running rate. The real bill can be lower, but it follows your usage.
- It works best if your app doesn't keep files on its own disk.
- A database is a separate paid service, not in this price unless the report says so.
- It's partly tied to Azure. Moving later is possible, but it takes work.

**A good fit if:**

- Your team or company already uses Azure
- A web app or API that doesn't keep files on its own disk
- A team that wants no servers or clusters to look after

**Think again if:**

- The app stores important files on its own disk
- Nobody on the team has used Azure and nobody wants to

**Before you launch**

- Set a budget alert in Azure, so a surprise charge reaches you.
- Use a separate service principal for deployments with only the permissions it needs.
- Check where the app writes files and move that elsewhere.
- Try a deploy in a test subscription first.

**What the download adds for this choice:** no infrastructure files exist for it yet, but you still get the basic files.

**Links**

- [Azure Container Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/products/container-apps)
- [Container Apps pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/container-apps/)

## Your chosen setup: One Hetzner Cloud server (CPX02: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM), excl. VAT

**In plain words.** You rent one small computer in a data centre and your app runs on it. It's like renting a flat yourself instead of staying in a hotel with staff.

**Cost.** About 6.49 EUR per month, from the report's price table (prices read 2026-10-24). Taxes, traffic charges and anything the report doesn't list aren't included.

**If the machine or its data centre has a problem:** this stops until it's fixed or recreated, because everything runs in one place.

**What you get**

- The lowest price in this list.
- Easy to understand: one machine runs your app, with no cluster or extra services to learn.
- A simple bill: it is mostly the price of the one machine you rent.
- Quick to set up: the download has what it takes to create the server and start your app.
- No lock-in: your app runs in plain Docker, so you can move it to another provider later.

**Why it costs what it does.** You only pay for the machine. The pricier options also pay for spare copies of your app, for switching over when something fails, and for someone else keeping it all running. Here none of that comes with it, so it costs less and that work lands on you.

**What you give up**

- If the machine breaks or restarts, your app is down until you sort it out. Nothing switches over by itself.
- Updates and security patches are yours to install.
- Backups are off unless you turn them on, and Hetzner charges extra for them.
- It can't grow by itself: a sudden rush makes it slow, and a bigger project will outgrow one machine.

**A good fit if:**

- A first launch, a side project or an internal tool
- Small, steady traffic
- A team that can log into a server and fix things

**Think again if:**

- You've promised customers almost no downtime
- Losing recent data would really hurt
- Nobody on the team is comfortable with a server
- Traffic is big or hard to predict

**Before you launch**

- Turn on backups, then restore one to see that it works.
- Set up an uptime alert, so you hear about it when the site is down.
- Pick a regular time to install updates.
- Keep the Terraform files: they can create the same machine again if you lose it (your data is separate).

**How this choice changes the gaps in your report**

- `no_observability`: Matters more on one machine, because nobody restarts it for you. Add an uptime alert before you launch.

**What the download adds for this choice**

- `infra/hetzner/main.tf`

- `infra/hetzner/cloud-init.yaml`
- `infra/hetzner/terraform.tfvars.example`
- `docker-compose.prod.yml`
- `deploy/Caddyfile`
